sources.title: Jim Cramer's top 10 things to watch in the stock market Friday
summaryHints: 96 Start your investing day with Jim's Morning thoughts.
VIEW IN BROWSER   |   LATEST CRAMER NEWS My top 10 things to watch Friday, April 17 1.
The  S&P 500  is headed for a higher open this morning after Iran  declared  the Strait of Hormuz open to commercial traffic during the Israel-Lebanon 10-day ceasefire.
President  Donald Trump  said the U.S.-Iran war "should be ending pretty soon." The S&P 500, which is on track for another winning week, closed at another record high in Thursday trading.
iPhone shipments in China  jumped 20%  during the first quarter, according to CounterPoint Research data.

items.title: Item 1
items.text: The S&P 500 is headed for a higher open this morning after Iran declared the Strait of Hormuz open to commercial traffic during the Israel-Lebanon 10-day ceasefire. Oil prices sank 10%. President Donald Trump said the U.S.-Iran war "should be ending pretty soon." The S&P 500, which is on track for another winning week, closed at another record high in Thursday trading.

items.title: Item 2
items.text: iPhone shipments in China jumped 20% during the first quarter, according to CounterPoint Research data. That was despite an overall decline in the smartphone market due to soaring memory costs. Great news for Apple's biggest money maker. I continue to say, "own, don't trade" this one.

items.title: Item 3
items.text: Price target came fast and furious cuts on Netflix. Barclays lowered to $110 from $115 after the company delivered disappointing guidance. Wolfe Research took Netflix down to $107 from $110. Rosenblatt cut to $95 from $96. Shares are down more than 9%.

items.title: Item 4
items.text: Bank of America swapped JPMorgan for Goldman Sachs in its best ideas list. Analysts kept their buy ratings on both. I still like Goldman. It is Wells Fargo that I tire of, especially after this week's lackluster earnings . We downgraded our Club rating on Wells Fargo to a hold-equivalent 2 . We own both Goldman and Wells.

items.title: Item 5
items.text: Danaher was taken from a price target of $220 to $205 at Rothschild & Co Redburn. Analysts said the company's exposure to its legacy stainless-steel Pall business will dampen growth. We exited Danaher in February. This is not the same old business that I have loved over the many years I have followed this one.

items.title: Item 6
items.text: JPMorgan trimmed its Procter & Gamble price target to $162 from $165. Analysts tweaked their estimates ahead of next week's earnings. They kept P&G a buy. But no enthusiasm there. We own P&G as a hedge against economic uncertainty. With a new CEO, I wished we owned more for the Club.

items.title: Item 7
items.text: Estee Lauder got a price target cut to $98 from $121 at JPMorgan, which also removed the stock from its analyst focus list but kept a buy rating. The troubled luxury brand reports earnings on May

items.title: Item 1
items.text: Maybe this company needs to sell itself? It's a broken stock.

items.title: Item 8
items.text: Affirm was elevated to a top pick at Morgan Stanley. Analysts cited "overdone" private credit concerns putting a drag on financials. They said next month's investor day meeting could be a catalyst for this buy-now-pay-later name whose stock can be volatile.

items.title: Item 9
items.text: Unheralded Prologis call. That's because of new CEO Dan Letter, who understated some of the good things happening at the industrial real estate company. Didn't tell the story of an uptick in rents or the data center build-out. Letter took over in January.

items.title: Item 10
items.text: Lots of price target cuts for Abbott Laboratories: Benchmark to $120 from $145, Stifel to $120 from $145, and Bank of America to $120 from $150. The prevailing view is that yesterday's earnings and conference call didn't wow the Street. However, analysts at all three firms did keep the stock a buy.

summaryHints: This company could be a big winner of the space race, the surge in defense spending, and several other major trends.
The Motley Fool - Stock Advisor NEW RECOMMENDATION ********************************************
* Moog: A Leader in Mission-Critical Components ********************************************

* By Tom Gardner • Stock Advisor Investing Type: Cautious “I like how Moog offers a potential sweet spot for exposure to the commercial space race -- broader end-market diversification than a pure play like Rocket Lab, with space more material to the story than it is at Amazon.

We hope this company can help Foolish investors reach new heights and steer toward long-term goals.” Loren Horst LOREN HORST Analyst, Stock Advisor There's a massive opportunity in the space economy right now.
